Smt. Geeta Saket vs Veerpal Singh Chouhan on 3 September,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:42596
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Himanshu Joshi
 On The 3 rd Of September, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 6071 of 2024
 Smt. Geeta Saket
 Versus
 Veerpal Singh Chouhan And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Abhay Sohgaura - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Himanshu Dwivedi - Advocate for respondent No.1.
 Shri Sanjeeev Kumar Mishra - Advocate for respondent No
 Order

The present miscellaneous appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, has been preferred by the appellant assailing the award dated 20.06.2024 passed by the 9th Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Rewa, in MACC No.126/2017, awarding compensation to the tune of Rs.15,000/- in favour of the appellant/claimant along with interest @6% per annum.
2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Rewa
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The facts of the case in short are that on 11.12.2014 at about 07:30 a.m., when the appellant was on the way to Govindgarh, near the turning of Govindgarh-Parasiya, the truck bearing No.
MP-19-HA-1491 being driven by respondent No.2 rashly and negligently hit the appellant, as a result of which, the deceased had sustained grievous injuries leading to permanent disability and filed a claim petition claiming compensation to the tune of Rs.10,00,000/-.
3.

The learned Tribunal has found that the accident was caused by respondent No.2 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle which was insured with respondent No.3 on the date of accident.
On account of said NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42596 2 MA-6071-2024 accident, the present appellant had sustained injuries and remained hospitalized for 05 days.
The learned Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.15,000/- in lump sum.
4. It is not disputed that respondent No.2 was responsible for causing the accident on the fateful day and the offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.3.
The only question of determination before this Court is as to whether the amount awarded by learned Tribunal requires modification/enhancement or not.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After hearing the rival submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, taking into account the nature of injuries, duration and intensity of pain, hospitalization period and the long-term effects on the claimant's lifestyle, this Court finds that the Tribunal has awarded the amount of compensation on lower side and the appellant is entitled to get the enhanced compensation to the tune of Rs.60,000/- in lump sum in place of Rs.15,000/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as has been awarded by the Tribunal.
6. Accordingly, the appeal stands partly allowed to the extent indicated above.
7. There shall be no order as to costs.

(HIMANSHU JOSHI) JUDGE Prachi Smt. Geeta Saket vs Veerpal Singh Chouhan on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180893339/
